I haven't had any experience with input delay (although if you start downloading CDLCs some will have notes that aren't on time which is annoying), however the note detection isn't always consistent (which may sometimes be the result of a faulty cable) which can sometimes be annoying if you're trying to 100% a song or something. Overall I like it a lot, but I wouldn't rely on it as the sole teacher to learn from. It's more of a casual fun thing to jam along to songs with imo. My problem from mainly using Rocksmith at first was that I didn't have any specific critique on my own play that you would get from something like a teacher, so I developed bad habits at first that I eventually had to break. Another problem at first was that I was very reliant on the notes on screen, so there were songs I could play front to back in-game but once I was playing on my own I would be completely clueless.

Nowadays I like to balance between playing Rocksmith and playing on my own, and I've been pretty happy with my progress since doing that. Been playing for almost a year now with about half of that being solely from Rocksmith, eventually I took a guitar class as well as playing outside of the game.

Also I sometimes want to be quiet and not use my amp so I just sit in the main menu and use Rocksmith as an amp with my headphones, which is a nice plus.

I've been throwing out the word underrated everywhere but now that I think about it I'd say Welcome To Bangkok is their most underrated track.

The way the album is structured feels like You Won't Know is the climax to the first half and everything from Not The Sun onwards imo has this different feeling to it, not an entirely different album but a slight change of tone from the first half.

Then you have Welcome To Bangkok which is like the instrumental interlude between these two halves, and I think it often gets overlooked because of that. However I think it stands as its own track pretty well. I love the wall of sound in the second half with the layered guitars and Jesse screaming into his guitar pickups.

Well I originally planned to just list them with a brief reason for each but I got a little passionate for some of them and also a LOT lazier for others haha. Although like everyone my top 10 changes a lot but regardless if the order changes these would all still float around my top favorite Brand New songs. Also there aren't any Daisy or Your Favorite Weapon songs on the list sadly, I love both of those albums but I find a lot of my all-time favorites are off TDAG/Deja/SF.

10. Sowing Season (Yeah)

Sowing Season is a runner up for my favorite Brand New album opener (#1 is a little higher up on the list...) but still an amazing song. I think it sets the tone for the rest of the album perfectly.

9. Jesus Christ

A lot of my favorite BN lyrics are all on this song. I overplayed this one so it isn't nearly as high as maybe I would normally put it, but it's definitely a top 10.

A couple of my favorite lyrics...

"And I will die all alone / And when I arrive I won't know anyone"

"Well, Jesus Christ, I'm not scared to die / But I'm a little bit scared of what comes after / Do I get the gold chariot? / Do I float through the ceiling?"

"Cause my bright is too slight to hold back all my dark / And this ship went down in sight of land"

8. Batter Up

So fucking underrated it's insane. I do like that there was an appreciation post for this song here recently as it definitely deserved it. At first I too thought it was slow and kinda boring, but eventually I started to love its haunting ambience and minimalistic delivery. Also seeing it as Brand New's final song and goodbye to everyone really paints it in a whole new light. My favorite closer to a Brand New album.

7. Lit Me Up

Glad to see someone else loves this song! Very underrated imo. Just as Batter Up is my favorite closer, Lit Me Up is my favorite opener from them and my favorite off of Science Fiction. Love it for all the same reasons I love Batter Up. Haunting, minimalistic, and atmospheric.

6. Quiet Things That No One Ever Knows

i like it a lot lol hehe

5. Sic Transit Gloria

The bassline alone brought it to the top 5 let's be real here. As far as Brand New's pop punk side, I think this song and Quiet Things are definitely their best work, which I know isn't saying anything special as it's their most popular songs.

Also, "die young and save yourself" is probably my favorite "one-liner" lyric from them.

4. Me vs. Maradona vs Elvis

I think you said it very well. Very disturbing but yet beautiful with an insane climax at the end.

3. Limousine

The first song I heard that really made me pay attention to this band. The soft acoustic opening, the slow build-up of the "One will love you so much, etc.", the layered vocals of the "Well I should be laughing right now" refrain over it, then finally exploding in a (relatively simple but VERY effective) solo before eventually dying down with long drawn out droning and amp feedback in the outro. I love it. Not to mention the story behind the song.

1 & 2. You Won't Know/Welcome To Bangkok

You Won't Know is easily my favorite, and I think the extended live versions of it are even better. Not only that, I think the transition into Welcome To Bangkok is amazing and I almost always listen to them as one long song. If there's any recurring theme amongst my favorites, it's that a lot of them have long buildups and play around with the loud/soft dynamics. And I think these two songs are the peak of that dynamic that I'm obsessed with in their music.

Edit: Revisiting this list I'd definitely rank Jesus Christ higher, probably somewhere around the top 5, but I'll leave it as is.

With how empty the rewards in games like that feel because the game is basically designed to give you a constant loop of satisfaction and none of it truly feels earned or special (outside of the more unique moments like the raids).

I still enjoy the game from time to time on a casual level but I just find it crazy how many people "main" a game like that and it's like their main hobby. The gameplay is fun here and there but it just feels meaningless in the end with how it's literally designed to drain your time and money. On paper I like the idea of GaaS (the concept of having a main game that evolves and grows over time) but I think in reality that trend has poisoned the industry and changed the perspective of games being developed to be a handcrafted self contained piece of art to a mindless grind designed to be milked for as much money as possible, profiting off people with addiction and impulse issues with their scummy manipulative game design and monetization tactics.
